---
title: Get started
description: Install biblioflow and run your first bibliometric workflow.
---

## Installation

Install the core library from PyPI:

```bash
pip install biblioflow
```

Optional YAML import/export support is provided as an extra:

```bash
pip install "biblioflow[yaml]"
```

Install application packages only when you need them:

```bash
pip install biblioflow-web
pip install biblioflow-nb
```

::: {.callout-note}
The applications depend on the core `biblioflow` package. New analysis features
should be implemented in the core library first and then exposed by the web and
notebook interfaces.
:::

## Load bibliographic records

```python
import biblioflow as bf

dataset = bf.load(
    "records.ris",
    provider="auto",
    format="auto",
)
```

`bf.load()` returns a `BibliographicDataset` containing normalized records,
raw records, metadata, warnings, and errors.

```python
len(dataset)
dataset.metadata
dataset.warning_dicts()
dataset.to_records()[:3]
```

## Supported input formats

| Format | Typical extension | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| RIS | `.ris` | Common export format from reference managers and scholarly databases. |
| BibTeX | `.bib` | Common for LaTeX and citation managers. |
| CSV/TSV | `.csv`, `.tsv` | Useful for spreadsheets and custom exports. |
| JSON/JSONL | `.json`, `.jsonl` | Supports generic records and provider payloads. |
| XML | `.xml` | Includes PubMed XML support. |
| NBIB | `.nbib` | PubMed/NLM text export format. |
| YAML | `.yaml`, `.yml` | Optional extra: `biblioflow[yaml]`. |

## Provider inference

Use `provider="auto"` and `format="auto"` for convenience, or pass explicit
values when working with known exports:

```python
dataset = bf.load("openalex.json", provider="openalex", format="json")
dataset = bf.load("pubmed.xml", provider="pubmed", format="xml")
dataset = bf.load("crossref.json", provider="crossref", format="json")
```

Provider-aware adapters normalize database-specific field names into the
canonical biblioflow schema.

## Descriptive analysis

```python
summary = bf.analyze(dataset, top_n=20)
summary.to_dict()
```

The descriptive summary includes high-level information, annual production,
top authors, top sources, and top keywords.

## Matrix and network construction

```python
keyword_matrix = bf.matrix(
    dataset,
    kind="co_occurrence",
    unit="keywords_all",
    normalize="association",
    min_occurrences=2,
)

keyword_network = bf.network(
    dataset,
    kind="co_occurrence",
    unit="keywords_all",
    normalize="association",
    min_occurrences=2,
)
```

## Export results

```python
bf.export(dataset, "records.json", format="json")
bf.export(keyword_matrix, "keywords.csv", format="csv")
bf.export(keyword_network, "keywords.graphml", format="graphml")
```

Supported network exports include JSON, GraphML, GEXF, Pajek, and
VOSviewer-style edge lists.

## Command-line interface

The command name is `biblioflow`:

```bash
biblioflow --help
biblioflow validate records.ris
biblioflow analyze records.ris --top-n 25 -o summary.json
biblioflow matrix records.ris -o keywords.csv --kind co_occurrence --unit keywords_all
biblioflow network records.ris -o network.graphml --to graphml
```

Do not use or document a hyphenated command alias.
